children: About half of actively managed U.S. large-cap stock funds beat their benchmarks in October, while growth managers and small-cap stock pickers posted stronger results, according to a Nov. 5 report by BofA Securities strategists Victoria Roloff and Savita Subramanian.

Some 49% of large-cap active funds outperformed, exceeding the historical monthly average of 46%. Results were mixed despite conditions that generally favored stock picking: 76% of stocks beat the S&P 500 (
), the highest share in the bank’s data history.

children: For investors weighing active funds against index products, the findings highlight the distinction between beating a benchmark and making money. Growth funds were more successful at outperforming during October’s sell-off, but still suffered losses. Value funds gained on average, yet most trailed their benchmark.
Among large-cap growth funds, 67% outperformed their benchmarks. The average fund fell 5.4%, beating its benchmark by 0.65 percentage point.
Diversified growth funds fared particularly well as mega-cap stocks lagged. Their outperformance rate reached 79%, compared with 49% for non-diversified growth funds.

Just 36% of large-cap core funds and 29% of value funds beat their benchmarks. Value funds returned an average of 3.3%, but faced a demanding comparison: the Russell 1000 Value Index outpaced its growth counterpart by more than 10 percentage points, the widest gap since February 2001.
Sector positioning also hurt large-cap active managers. Energy and consumer staples, among October’s strongest sectors, were relatively under-owned, according to the report.
Small-cap funds benefit from quality rebound

Small-cap active managers delivered the strongest results, with 75% beating their benchmarks. They exceeded the outperformance rates of both large-cap and mid-cap funds for a second consecutive month.
The bank attributed that strength partly to renewed leadership by higher-quality companies within the Russell 2000
. Small-cap active funds typically favor quality and profitability, making that shift supportive of their holdings.
Mid-cap managers also performed well, with 66% outperforming in October.
Through October, 40% of large-cap active funds were ahead of their benchmarks. That compares with 29% for last year and an annual average of 37% since the early 2000s.

Among mid-cap funds, 55% were outperforming their Russell benchmarks this year, compared with 48% of small-cap funds. Despite October’s stronger showing in those categories, sustained benchmark outperformance remained far from universal, according to BofA.

title: Growth funds limit losses as active managers deliver mixed October results, BofA says
